title: Asyncio Core Concepts (Event Loop, Coroutines, Tasks)

slides.title: Asynchronous Programming with `asyncio`
slides.prompt: Asyncio uses single-threaded single-process cooperative multitasking via an event loop. Functions declared with `async def` are coroutines, yielding control back to the event loop using `await`.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio

async def fetch_data():
    print("Start fetching")
    await asyncio.sleep(1)  # Non-blocking pause
    print("Data fetched")
    return {"data": 1}

async def main():
    result = await fetch_data()
    print(result)

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Non-blocking Sleep
slides.prompt: Why MUST you use `await asyncio.sleep()` instead of `time.sleep()` inside an asyncio coroutine?
options: `time.sleep()` blocks the entire event loop thread, stopping all other concurrent tasks
`time.sleep()` raises a CoroutineTypeError inside async functions
`asyncio.sleep()` uses multiple CPU cores for sleeping
`time.sleep()` causes immediate garbage collection of the loop
slides.correctAnswer: `time.sleep()` blocks the entire event loop thread, stopping all other concurrent tasks
